name: 23 (2026-11-25 evening)
what: analysis round on the queue entries that ended during the day: A (its chain, the Szekeres series, the smoothed-edge member), B (mesh leg and particle leg), E (the G3 pilot, then the baseline), core (queue order for the release checks, row 4, A's question on the PCS cloud, the merge of the next release prepared)
note: Releases core-v0.4 to v0.7 are on main. Rulings: coord/DECISIONS/0037 to 0042. The cards came back on 2026-11-25 at 09:49 PST and ten more queue entries have ended since. After git merge main: nrpic-run finish closes runs continued in place; finish and verify keep a checksum cache (the first pass reads everything once: start it in the background and do not wait; one pass with --full before a gate review). Every new run that uses the horizon finder sets <fastflow> diagnostics = true; horizons are read from the status file where it exists (0040 item 3). The week's usage is tight (0040 item 5): keep to the time given, read what the task needs. Close a finished run before you analyse it; every number with its run id; prediction before every new run; figures made by registered scripts and looked at; at most 6 cores.

items.extra: Extra for this session (about seventy-five minutes). Ended since your last session: queue entries q0013 a-p0l6 (the chain reached its end), q0040 a-szk-n64-128 and q0041 a-szk-n256; and your detached processor runs: the smoothed members S2c-A and S2c-B (A-20261125-161154-62ce3dc), the PCS twin (A-20261125-160633-594a474), N-z128 (A-20261125-160633-e38d321). (1) Close each and judge it against its predictions with a registered analysis and a figure you look at: P0L6 (D1 to D5; the first find at t = 118.1 read critically from the status file); the Szekeres series (P17 to P21); the finer-mesh member of the smoothed-edge test, and then item C3 as rulings 0039 item 2(c), 0040 item 6 and 0041 item 2 say (does the violation fall with the mesh, and at what order?); N-z128 for test A2. (2) The control that separates a relativistic lag from a coordinate effect in S1L: first a crossing measure that does not depend on the coordinates, from the snapshots that exist; a new card member only if that cannot decide (prediction first, priority 2). (3) The G2 package item by item. If what remains open is only failures on record with their rulings and items that wait for the fresh verifier of the whole gate, write the G2 sections of the note, the schematics on the release and the rerun list, run nrpic-stage collect, verify and report, and list G2 in gates_complete so that the verifier and the gate review can be sent; otherwise say which queue entry each open item waits for.

Extra for this session (about seventy-five minutes). The pilot of G3 has ended (queue entry q0050 G3P: run id with nrpic-queue show q0050); q0051 G3C and q0052 G3R wait; the zeta reader may judge G3 runs (decision 0042 item 1; g3/zeta_verify/VERIFY.md). (1) The verifier's two changes to the tests: Z1 along the momentum alone recorded as a failure of the reference with the variational coefficients as expected values; expected values taken at the box's own background at N_f. (2) Close the pilot and read it against the predictions of g3/JOURNAL.md entries 2 and 4 with your reader; compare the two readers cell by cell on one pilot dump (g3/zeta_verify/scripts/zv_lib.py reads 128-cell dumps: about ten minutes on one core); the measured cost per seed into scope 4d.9 A12; figures. (3) If the pilot holds: queue the remaining baseline pairs and the level-2 pairs through the shared queue, several pairs per job, six new entries at most; if it does not hold, say what failed and queue nothing. (4) Stage G3: collect and say what the gate lacks.

items.task: Round for core without a change of athenak/src or python/nrpic (about seventy-five minutes). (1) Queue order: the card checks of the releases wait behind the row-4 members because the queue takes core's entries by age: q0049 (branch core/restart-finder, the next release), q0039, q0035, q0036 (core-v0.7). Remove the row-4 entries of core that still wait (nrpic-queue list; note each one's arguments with nrpic-queue show first) and add them again after the four checks have been dispatched, or at the end of this session with --after the last check; say what you did. Do not touch entries that are in Slurm. (2) Row 4, level 3: q0029, q0030, q0031 have ended: close them, fates by the rule, the bracket, the figure; the 0.726875 member with its control now. (3) Track A asks (its outbox pcs-deposit-refinement-boundary; rulings 0041 item 2) whether the residual of the Hamiltonian constraint that the PCS cloud leaves at boundaries of static refinement on an initial slice is a property of the scheme or a defect (with CIC the residual is twenty times smaller and converges). Read the deposit across refinement levels in the source, make one small processor test that could show a defect (a uniform lattice across a refinement boundary: is the deposited density uniform to round-off for CIC, TSC and PCS, with and without <particles> deposit_fine_shape?), prediction first, figure; answer A. If it is a defect, put it at the head of tracks/core/NEXT_SOURCE.md with the test. (4) Tracks D and F ask that <fastflow> diagnostics can be switched on in a run continued from a restart file (decision 0042 item 4): add it to NEXT_SOURCE.md with the place in the source and a test. (5) Prepare, do not release: merge origin/core/restart-finder into core/nrpic on processors (the changelog sections may collide), build, byte regression (75 items) and the quick tests; the release waits for the card check q0049, which you judge with tracks/core/analysis/restart_finder/card_check.py if it has run (journal entry 20 of JOURNAL-restart-finder.md has the command). Records, commit, push core/nrpic.
